scope: Period reconstruction of GBA raster timing and the AGS-101 board-to-panel interface without access to an authentic motherboard, panel, or synchronized measurement rig.
rules: Exact GBA raster constants may be formal constants when a period manufacturer document and an independent technical reconstruction agree.
An artifact photograph establishes only the markings and construction visible in that artifact.
A manufacturer-family document can establish signal semantics but not AGS-101-specific phase, voltage, or topology.
AGS-001 topology is never promoted to AGS-101 fact without a separately recorded transfer argument.
A failed exact-part search is evidence of an unresolved field, not evidence that a nearby part is equivalent.
Emulator execution validates ROM compatibility and the scene contract, not original hardware timing.

items.title: Nintendo Game Boy Advance Programming Manual, version 1.35
items.preservation: third-party mirror of a Nintendo period document
claimsUsed: 240 visible and 308 total dots per line
160 visible and 228 total lines per frame
68 horizontal-blank dots and 68 vertical-blank lines
73.433 microseconds per line, 16.743 milliseconds per frame, and 59.727 hertz as rounded published values
Mode 4 defines two 240 by 160 indexed-color frame buffers
items.limits: The document does not identify the AGS-101 panel latch edge, VCOM phase, inversion topology, or optical delay. The hosting site is not Nintendo.

items.title: GBATEK GBA LCD timing, CPU pinout, and GBA SP display socket
claimsUsed: four CPU cycles per dot, 1232 cycles per line, and 280896 cycles per frame
the generic GBA SP display socket exposes DCK, LP, PS, SPL, CLS, SPS, MOD, REVC, RGB data buses, panel supplies, and COM
the GBA SP CPU pinout names the corresponding LCD-interface signals
items.limits: This is technical reverse engineering, not Nintendo electrical documentation. The generic GBA SP interface map is not direct proof of the AGT-CPU-01 routing, edge polarity, voltage, or timing.

items.title: AGS-101 XU70954250-4 artifact record
claimsUsed: one recorded 2005 AGS-101 contains a C/AGT-CPU-01 motherboard
the same recorded unit carries panel sticker LQ029B1DC01F 58E06466754 and panel stamp 0026 050820
the board carries a CPU AGB B E marked Nintendo and manufactured by Sharp
items.limits: One community-curated photographed specimen establishes identity markings only. It is not an electrical trace, optical measurement, or Sharp panel datasheet.

items.title: Game Boy hardware database AGS artifact index
claimsUsed: multiple archived AGS-101 units are photographed with C/AGT-CPU-01 motherboards
archived AGT board records span multiple serials and manufacture years
items.limits: Board photography supports identity and visual topology only; it does not establish hidden routing, component values, or panel timing.

items.title: Reverse-engineered AGS-CPU-11 schematic
claimsUsed: an AGS-001 board provides a period-adjacent example of SP display-interface and power topology
the repository documents component identification by desoldering and measurement
items.limits: The author explicitly says the schematic is accurate only for AGS-CPU-11. It cannot establish an AGT-CPU-01 net, component value, phase, or inversion mode.

items.title: Sharp LZ9JG17B TFT-LCD timing-controller datasheet
claimsUsed: DCK is a data clock in the documented Sharp controller family
LP and source-driver timing are distinct from CLS and SPS gate-driver timing
REVC is associated with preparation for common-electrode drive
items.limits: LZ9JG17B is not identified as the AGS-101 controller. Its dimensions, edge polarities, frequencies, and phase values are not transferred.

items.title: GBA Frame Test ROM and original-display high-speed examples
claimsUsed: original GBA-family displays show a line-by-line scan pattern in high-speed video
items.limits: The repository supplies qualitative examples, not synchronized timing metrology or an AGS-101-specific edge measurement.

items.title: Pinned mGBA WS2 ROM smoke and independent scene consistency receipt
claimsUsed: all eleven generated ROMs boot in the pinned mGBA executable
ROM headers, code probes, palettes, framebuffer pages, page-selection writes, and dwell literals match the WS2 source and manifest
items.limits: The receipt does not observe original hardware signals or AGS-101 optical output.

items.title: Exact LQ029B1DC01F specification search
items.result: No exact manufacturer specification or traceable exact-part datasheet was located in the checked web and archive indexes.
items.limits: Absence from this search does not prove that no specification exists. Nearby LQ029 or LQ030 part numbers are explicitly excluded as exact substitutes.

items.title: GBA2-DLF reverse-engineering design note
items.limits: The note labels key LCD-interface interpretation as uncertain. It is retained in the search log but excluded from formal constants and phase selection.
